sections.title: Foundations of Robotic Manipulation
sections.description: This course covers algorithms, mathematical models and computational frameworks that enable autonomous robotic decision-making and manipulation in everyday environments. Topics of this course include: the mechanics of contact and friction, grasping, force and tactile sensing, motion planning, learning-based motion generation, manipulator control, task and motion planning, learned models, planning under uncertainty, manipulation benchmarks and simulators. Students will engage with foundational principles as well as state of the art research through paper readings, reviews and presentations and an independent final project. Prerequisite: This is an advanced robotics course designed for graduate students. Students are expected to have a solid foundation in robot kinematics (MEAM 5200 or equivalent). For the final project, programming experience is required to implement, apply or extend a manipulation algorithm. While Python is recommended due to the ubiquity of libraries and codebases, you may use the programming language of your choice. Prior exposure to the basic concepts of linear algebra, algorithms, and machine learning is strongly recommended.
